This represents the derivative of the Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss with respect to the rendered pixel value [S2].

The claim states that the evidence represents the derivative of the Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss with respect to the rendered pixel value. The evidence explicitly defines the MSE loss as Loss = (1/N) Σ ||L_out - L_tag||^2. It then computes the difference term diff = 2(L_out[i,j] - L_tag[i,j]). Mathematically, the derivative of (L_out - L_tag)^2 with respect to L_out is 2(L_out - L_tag). The evidence uses this term (diff) as the gradient of the loss with respect to the rendered pixel value (L_out) before scattering it to the density field. Therefore, the term 'diff' or the gradient component derived from it represents the derivative of the MSE loss with respect to the rendered pixel value.

It solves the inverse problem of recovering physical density from observed images by computing the gradient of a loss function with respect to voxel values and applying gradient descent [S2].

The claim states that the method solves the inverse problem of recovering physical density from observed images by computing the gradient of a loss function with respect to voxel values and applying gradient descent. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly confirms this: Section 3.4 describes optimizing the density field ρ using Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss between target and rendered images. It details the computation of the gradient ∂Loss/∂ρ[vp] via chain rule and scattering, and explicitly states the update step using gradient descent: ρ[vp] ← ρ[vp] − α ∂Loss/∂ρ[vp]. Thus, every part of the claim is supported by the text.

While `densityGrad` is an array indexed by voxels and thus logically has size proportional to the number of voxels, the provided evidence text does not explicitly state or quantify the memory complexity of `densityGrad` as $O(N_{voxels})$. It mentions initializing it to zero and updating it, but does not provide the specific complexity analysis for this variable's storage in the context of the claim. Therefore, only part of the claim is explicitly supported by the text.
